questions.q: Whose family history does this passage record?
questions.a: This passage records the family history of Aaron and Moses.

questions.q: What were the names of Aaron’s sons?
questions.a: The names of Aaron’s sons were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

questions.q: What work did the sons of Aaron do, the ones who were anointed?
questions.a: The sons of Aaron were the priests. They were anointed and set apart to serve as priests.

questions.q: Why did Nadab and Abihu die in front of Yahweh?
questions.a: Nadab and Abihu died in front of Yahweh when they offered strange fire to him.

questions.q: Which of Aaron’s sons served as priests with Aaron?
questions.a: Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests with their father Aaron.

questions.q: Which tribe did Yahweh say was to help Aaron serve as priest?
questions.a: The tribe of Levi was to help Aaron.

questions.q: What were the duties of the tribe of Levi?
questions.a: They were to do the work for Aaron and for all the Israelites at the tent of meeting, take care of all the equipment of the tent of meeting, and serve at the Dwelling.

questions.q: Whom did Yahweh tell Moses to give to Aaron and his sons?
questions.a: Yahweh told Moses to give the Levites to Aaron and his sons. The Levites were given to Aaron from among the Israelites.

questions.q: Whom did Yahweh set apart for himself?
questions.a: Yahweh took the Levites for himself instead of the firstborn of Israel. He also set apart for himself every firstborn in Israel, both people and animals.

questions.q: When did Yahweh set apart all the firstborn of Israel for himself?
questions.a: He set apart for himself all the firstborn in Israel on the day that he struck down all the firstborn in the land of Egypt.

questions.q: Where did Yahweh speak to Moses when he told him to count the sons of Levi?
questions.a: Yahweh spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai.

questions.q: Whom did Yahweh command Moses to count in the tribe of Levi?
questions.a: Yahweh commanded Moses to count every male in Levi who was one month old or older.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Levi?
questions.a: The sons of Levi were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Gershon?
questions.a: The sons of Gershon were Libni and Shimei.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Kohath?
questions.a: The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.

questions.q: Who were the sons of Merari?
questions.a: The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi.

questions.q: Which two clans came from Gershon?
questions.a: The clan of the Libnites and the clan of the Shimeites came from Gershon.

questions.q: How many Gershonite males who were one month old or older did Moses count?
questions.a: Moses counted 7,500 Gershonite males who were one month old or older.

questions.q: Where were the clans of the Gershonites to camp?
questions.a: The clans of the Gershonites were to camp behind the Dwelling, on the west side.

questions.q: Who was the leader of the ancestral family of the Gershonites?
questions.a: Eliasaph the son of Lael was the leader of the ancestral family of the Gershonites.

questions.q: Who was to take care of the Dwelling, the tent and its covering, the curtains, the hangings of the courtyard, and the ropes?
questions.a: The sons of Gershon were to take care of the Dwelling, the tent and its covering, the curtains, the hangings of the courtyard, and the ropes.

questions.q: Which four clans came from Kohath?
questions.a: The clans of the Amramites, the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites came from Kohath.

questions.q: How many Kohathite males who were one month old or older did Moses count? What did they do?
questions.a: Moses counted 8,600 Kohathite males who were one month old or older. They were the keepers of the holy place.

questions.q: Where were the clans of the sons of Kohath to camp?
questions.a: The clans of the sons of Kohath were to camp on the south side of the Dwelling.

questions.q: Who was the leader of the ancestral family of the clans of the Kohathites?
questions.a: Elizaphan the son of Uzziel was the leader of the ancestral family of the clans of the Kohathites.

questions.q: What were the clans of Kohath, who camped on the south side of the Dwelling, to take care of?
questions.a: They were to take care of the box, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the vessels of the holy place, and the curtain.

questions.q: Who was Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest to supervise?
questions.a: He was to supervise the leaders of the Levites and the men who took care of the holy place.

questions.q: Which two clans came from Merari?
questions.a: The clan of the Mahlites and the clan of the Mushites came from Merari.

questions.q: How many Merarite males who were one month old or older did Moses count?
questions.a: Moses counted 6,200 Merarite males who were one month old or older.

questions.q: Who was to lead the clans of Merari, who camped on the north side of the Dwelling?
questions.a: Zuriel the son of Abihail was to lead the clans of Merari.

questions.q: What were the clans of Merari, who camped on the north side of the Dwelling, to take care of?
questions.a: They were to take care of the frames of the Dwelling, its crossbars, pillars, bases, and all its vessels, and the pillars, bases, pegs, and ropes of the courtyard.

questions.q: What were Moses, Aaron, and Aaron’s sons, who camped on the east side of the Dwelling, to do?
questions.a: They were to take care of the holy place and to do the duties that belonged to the Israelites.

questions.q: What was to happen to anyone who was not a Levite and who came near the holy place?
questions.a: That person was to be put to death.

questions.q: Whom did Moses and Aaron count?
questions.a: Moses and Aaron counted every male of the Levites who was one month old or older. The total was 22,000.

questions.q: Whom did Yahweh tell Moses to count among the sons of Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh told Moses to count every firstborn male of the sons of Israel who was one month old or older.

questions.q: Whom did Yahweh tell Moses to take for him instead of the firstborn of Israel and instead of their animals?
questions.a: Yahweh told Moses to take the Levites and the animals of the Levites instead of the firstborn of Israel and their animals.

questions.q: Then whom did Moses count?
questions.a: Moses counted all the firstborn males of Israel by name, who were one month old or older. The total was 22,273.

questions.q: To whom did all the Levites belong?
questions.a: The Levites belonged to Yahweh.

questions.q: How much silver did Yahweh tell Moses to take for each of the 273 firstborn males who were more than the number of the Levites?
questions.a: Yahweh told Moses to take five shekels for each one. He was to use the shekel of the holy place.

questions.q: To whom did Yahweh tell Moses to give the silver for the ransoms?
questions.a: Yahweh told Moses to give the silver to Aaron and his sons.

questions.q: From whom did Moses take the silver of the ransom?
questions.a: Moses took the silver from the firstborn who were more than the number of the Levites.

questions.q: How much silver did Moses take from the firstborn of the sons of Israel?
questions.a: Moses took 1,365 shekels of silver, by the shekel of the holy place.

questions.q: To whom did Moses give the silver for the ransom of the firstborn of Israel?
questions.a: He gave the silver to Aaron and his sons, as Yahweh had commanded.

commentary.text: The sons of Aaron, The Levites taken instead of the first-born.
The Levites numbered by their families, Their duties.

Verses 1–13 There was much work belonging to the priests' office, and there were now only Aaron and his two sons to do it; God appoints the Levites to attend them. Those whom God finds work for, he will find help for. The Levites were taken instead of the first-born. When He that made us, saves us, as the first-born of Israel were saved, we are laid under further obligations to serve him faithfully. God's right to us by redemption, confirms the right he has to us by creation.

The Levites were in three classes, according to the sons of Levi; Gershon, Kohath, and Merari; and these were subdivided into families. The posterity of Moses were not at all honoured or privileged, but stood upon the level with other Levites; thus it was plain, that Moses did not seek the advancement of his own family, or to secure any honours to it. The tribe of Levi was by much the least of all the tribes. God's chosen are but a little flock in comparison with the world.

The number of the first-born, and that of the Levites, came near to each other. Known unto God are all his works beforehand; there is an exact proportion between them, and so it will appear, when they are compared together. The small number of first-born, over and above the number of the Levites, were to be redeemed, and the redemption-money given to Aaron. The church is called the church of the first-born, which is redeemed, not as they were, with silver and gold; but, being devoted by sin to the justice of God, is ransomed with the precious blood of the Son of God. All men are the Lord's by creation, and all true christians are his by redemption. Each should know his own post and duty; nor can any service required by such a Master be rightly accounted mean or hard.
